render.stationsManifestPrelude: # cpm22 (slot 206) -- CP/M 2.2 on a Kaypro II, host-native MAME kayproii; cpm22 wave 2026-09-20.

museum.blurb: The A> prompt before DOS: CP/M 2.2 on a Z80 Kaypro II, where drive letters, command-line tools and WordStar were already familiar office computing years before the IBM PC won the market.
museum.notes: Host-native station: MAME's kayproii driver (bios 149c, board 81-110) runs on the host -- drawshm frames, ctlsock keys through the generated keymap, no audio and no network. Boots straight to the CP/M 2.2 (GMv2.72) A> prompt with a period software directory already staged on the boot floppy; WordStar 3.3 is a second floppy (flop2). Keyboard-only exhibit like apple2e/samcoupe/mpf2 -- the Kaypro II's own keyboard is HLE'd via an Intel i8048 MCU (device kayproiikbd), not a CPU-scanned matrix the driver owns directly. MEASURED 2026-09-20: a `DIR` typed cleanly with no drops at 80/80 ms pacing and no KEY_EXCL on the fleet-pinned 0.289 binary; the real-browser proof is the authority for production.

reset.mouse: N/A -- keyboard-only exhibit (pointer transport none), no mouse card or port on this machine.
reset.keyboard: MEASURED 2026-09-20 against the ACTUAL fleet-pinned mame0289 native binary (sandbox rig, sha256-verified kaypro_ii-ins8048.bin ROM, kayproiikbd device): `DIR` sent via POST + CODE {ENTER} re-ran the directory listing cleanly with no dropped/duplicated characters. SH_KEY_MIN_HOLD_MS/GAP=80/80 ms shipped per the fleet's MAME-keyboard rule. MAME_CTL_KEY_EXCL not set -- this driver's keyboard is HLE'd via a separate Intel i8048 MCU device (kayproiikbd), not a CPU-scanned matrix the driver polls directly; the real-browser typing proof is the authority on whether that holds under a production burst.
reset.fixture: Kaypro II CP/M 2.2 (GMv2.72) boot floppy (TOSEC preservation image, fed to MAME as .td0 -- MAME reads TeleDisk/ImageDisk natively, no raw conversion) -- boots straight to the A> prompt with the disk's own STANDARD PRINTER software directory already visible (ASM/BAUD/DDT/DUMP/ED/LOAD/... utilities, no visitor action needed). WordStar 3.3 (TOSEC .imd) is staged as a second floppy. MEASURED 2026-09-20 against the fleet-pinned 0.289 native binary: cold boot to the A> prompt in ~6 emulated seconds; golden savestate captured and restore-proven at that prompt (see reset.snapshot). Golden: sta/kayproii/golden.sta, 14338 bytes, sha256 bba86537a6a02963ddecdd908e6ed22cc02708852310a4716c1bff54f4ae4bd5 -- captured at the settled A> prompt (flop1 cpm22-boot.td0 attached), restore-proven on a FRESH process relaunch (PIL ImageChops.difference bbox None against the captured frame), 2026-09-20.

cpm22 wave 2026-09-20: driver is `kayproii`, NOT `kaypro2` as the integration seed guessed -- `kaypro2` is only formats/kaypro_dsk.cpp's floppy-format name string. Confirmed against a stock MAME 0.276 system package's -listxml on labhost.

media does not need raw .kay conversion: MAME reads the TOSEC .td0/.imd preservation images directly, and a dsktrans raw conversion of the same TD0 booted to a permanent 'insert diskette' prompt (bad logical sector order) -- see scripts/build-guests/tiles/cpm22.sh.

cpm22 wave resume 2026-09-20: sourced kaypro_ii-ins8048.bin (sha1 7919385fe8badbb610b793a3f5e4077982094aaa, matches the driver's own -listxml exactly) from archive.org item mame-roms-split (MAME 0.280 ROMs (split)), which serves each romset as a plain downloadable file -- unlike the mame-bios-devices mega-zip's zip-in-zip view_archive.php path, which 503'd then 404'd on the exact member. Re-ran the boot gate against the ALREADY-BUILT mame0289 binary (no rebuild); floor lowered 4000->2500 (measured 3163 lit px on the real 1024x768 drawshm surface, cold no-floppy banner). Golden savestate captured + restore-proven; real keymap dumped via mame-keymap.py (76 keys, replacing the stale apple2gs placeholder); MAME_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT flipped to 1.
